Can someone who has received a full presidential pardon still plead the Fifth Amendment when questioned about the conduct covered by the pardon?


A pardon protects you from federal prosecution, but it completely strips away your Fifth Amendment right to remain silent. 

Because you can no longer be prosecuted, a court or congressional committee can legally force you to testify about every detail of the crime.

This exact trap played out when Senator Josh Hawley questioned Dr. Anthony Fauci. 

After Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment to avoid answering even basic questions—like what color the carpet was—Hawley pointed out the legal reality. 

Because Fauci had received a pre-emptive pardon from Joe Biden, his Fifth Amendment privilege was legally gone.

If you accept a pardon, refusing to testify can land you in jail for contempt. 

If you lie under oath, you can be prosecuted for perjury—a brand-new crime your pardon won’t cover.
